title: could / couldn't – past ability
grammarNote: COULD — это прошедшее время глагола CAN. Используется для описания умений и способностей в ПРОШЛОМ: что ты умел/мог делать раньше. Как и CAN, глагол COULD одинаков для всех лиц и никогда не изменяется. После COULD стоит базовый инфинитив без 'to'.

grammarTable.subject: I / You
grammarTable.example: I could swim at age 6. · You could speak Kazakh fluently.

grammarTable.subject: He / She / It
grammarTable.example: She could dance at 4. · He could play chess as a child.

grammarTable.subject: We / They
grammarTable.example: We could stay up late. · They could run very fast.

grammarTable.subject: I / You
grammarTable.example: I couldn't read at 3. · You couldn't drive last year.

grammarTable.subject: He / She / It
grammarTable.example: She couldn't swim. · He couldn't speak English before.

grammarTable.subject: We / They
grammarTable.example: We couldn't be late. · They couldn't afford it.

grammarTable.subject: Could + subject + verb?
grammarTable.example: Could you run fast as a child? · Could she speak English at 10?

grammarTable.subject: Short answers
grammarTable.example: Yes, I could. / No, I couldn't. · Yes, she could. / No, he couldn't.

rows.form: I could walk at 1 year old.
rows.example: I could walk before I could talk!
She could sing perfectly at the age of five.
He could beat adults at chess when he was 8.
As children they could speak Kazakh fluently.

rows.form: We could stay up until midnight.
rows.example: We could stay up late in the summer holidays.
Kamila could play the dombra when she was eight.
I couldn't read yet when I started school.
She couldn't drive last year — she just passed her test.
He couldn't speak English at all before university.
They couldn't afford it on a student budget.
We couldn't find the address and arrived late.
He could not attend the exam. (formal writing)
PAST: I couldn't speak English two years ago.
PAST: She could only swim 500m last year.

rows.form: NOW: He can code in Python.
rows.example: PAST: He could only code in Scratch as a child.
PAST: They couldn't drive before last summer.

rows.form: NOW: We can stay up late.
rows.example: PAST: We could stay up all night as teenagers!
PAST: She could only play 3 songs at first.
✅ She could speak French. — COULD не меняется!
✅ I could swim. — После COULD нет "to"!
✅ He couldn't swim. — Базовая форма, не прошедшее!
✅ Could she dance? — Базовая форма в вопросе!

grammarTip:
could = прошедшее время can:
→ I can swim NOW. · I could swim AT AGE 5.
→ She can speak English NOW. · She couldn't speak English LAST YEAR.

Три правила could (такие же, как у can!):
① COULD не меняется: I could · She could · They could (НЕ 'she coulds'!)
② После COULD — базовый глагол: could swim · could dance (НЕ 'could to swim', НЕ 'could swam'!)
③ Отрицание: couldn't = could not.

exercises.text: Kamila ___ play the dombra when she was eight years old.
exercises.hint: Past ability → could. (when she was eight = past)

exercises.text: Amir ___ speak English well before university — he practised a lot.
She CAN swim 2km. → She ___ only swim 500m last year.
exercises.hint: "Only 500m" suggests limited past ability → could + couldn't.

exercises.text: "She coulds dance as a child" is correct.
exercises.hint: COULD never takes -s. → She could dance.
Short answer to a Could-question: Yes, he could.

opts: She could dance as a child.
exercises.hint: NEVER use "to" after could! → He could play chess.

exercises.text: Год назад она не умела водить машину.
exercises.hint: Past negative + base verb: couldn't drive.

opts: They could run very fast as children.
exercises.correct: They could run very fast as children.
exercises.hint: "They could run" ✅ — could + base verb. Others wrongly use past tense or add "to".

questions.text: What is the past form of CAN?
questions.hint: The past of CAN is COULD.

questions.text: She ___ swim at age 3 — she was amazing!
"He coulds play chess" — what is wrong?
questions.hint: COULD never changes form. → He could play chess.

questions.text: "I couldn't to speak English last year" is correct.
questions.hint: No 'to' after couldn't! → I couldn't speak English.

questions.text: How do you say "Раньше я не умел читать"?
questions.hint: Past negative ability → I couldn't + base verb.

questions.text: Kamila ___ play 20 songs now, but she ___ only play 3 when she started.
questions.hint: Now = can; Past (when she started) = could.
COULD + base infinitive (not past tense, no "to").
After Could → base form: Could she dance?

questions.text: Choose the correct translation: "Он не умел водить год назад."
As a child, Zhibek ___ do gymnastics, but she ___ do a backflip — she learned it later.
questions.hint: could = general ability in past; couldn't = specific thing she couldn't do.

questions.text: COULD is used to talk about ability in the present.
questions.hint: COULD is the PAST of CAN — it talks about past ability.

questions.text: Which uses COULD correctly for past ability?
opts: She could ran fast as a child.
He could speak three languages as a teenager.
questions.correct: He could speak three languages as a teenager.

questions.text: Before I studied English I ___ understand films, but now I ___!
questions.hint: Past negative → couldn't; Present positive → can.

questions.text: "I could speak Kazakh when I was 2." — When did this happen?
questions.hint: "when I was 2" — this is clearly in the past → could is correct.
